To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the general and specific factors in reading comprehension are the same, (2) general and specific factors are not the same, (3) general and specific fac tors are not the same.

(1) the reading comprehension of the 12th graders is not significantly different from that of the 6th graders, (2) the reading comprehension ability of 6th grad ers is not significantly different in the two languages, and (3) the 6th grade reading comprehension ability of students with English and Spanish as the home language is not significantly different.

(1) reading achievement is a product of general reading ability and specific reading ability; (2) general reading ability is a product of verbal intelligence and general scholastic ability; and (3) specific reading ability is a function of general reading ability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of the reading process and the factors that contribute to the reading problem.
the identification of general and spe cific factors which contribute to reading success.
the identification of the general and specific factors involved in the reading comprehension of high school seniors.

reading is the most important single factor in determining success in the elementary and secondary school curricula.

reading is a complex and difficult task which involves a number of skills, attitudes, and habits.

reading is a complex of skills which are interdependent.
reading has become a problem in all schools.
the reading problem is a complex one and that the solution of the problem must involve a number of interrelated factors.

the more we know about reading comprehension, the more we can do about it.
